title.narrative: Emergency WASH Response for Timely Action in the West Bank – 48-Hour

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed project will deliver a three-month emergency WASH intervention for forcibly displaced households and at-risk communities affected by settler-related violence, military operations, displacement, and damage to essential infrastructure in the West Bank. The intervention targets ltbgt423 families, approximately 2,200 individuals, in the Jordan Valley, Hebron, Tubas, Qalqilya and Ramallah.lt/bgtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe project combines immediate life-saving WASH assistance with targeted infrastructure improvements where a more sustainable solution is technically feasible. Core activities include ltbgtwater trucking, installation of HDPE pipelines and booster pumps, distribution and installation of PE water storage tanks, installation of mobile latrines with handwashing facilities, provision of hygiene kitslt/bgt with basic hygiene messaging, provision of metallic mobile water tankers, and deployment of solid waste containers.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtWhere feasible, particularly in Al Nwei'meh, Ein Fares, Ein Shibly, Beit Amin and Khallet Al Fouleh, PARC will install HDPE carrier lines and booster pumps as a safer, more reliable, and more affordable alternative to prolonged water trucking. Water trucking will continue as an interim measure until installation works are completed and the systems become operational.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe project will be implemented through rapid deployment, protection-sensitive siting, community coordination, and close coordination with OCHA field teams, WASH Cluster actors, municipalities, local councils, and community representatives. PARC's MEAL team will conduct regular monitoring, distribution checks, functionality checks, beneficiary feedback collection, and post-distribution monitoring to ensure accountability and timely adaptation.ltbrgtlt/pgt
